creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`muster pane send --enter` promises "Press Return afterwards, which is what submits it". It exits 0 whether or not anything was submitted, and against a harness that reads the text as a paste, nothing is.

Muster cannot fix the receiving harness and should not special-case one. What it can do is stop reporting success it has not got, and say so in `muster docs limits`. This card is where instances go until there are enough of them to decide which.

## Measured: Claude Code, 2026-08-31

An agent in one pane handing over to an agent in another, both Claude Code, Muster 0.1.1:

    muster pane send --pane p2025excth "<1583 bytes, one line, no newlines>" --enter
    exit 0

The text arrived in the receiving pane's input box as `[Pasted text #2]` and sat there unsubmitted until a person pressed Return. The sending agent had no way to tell: exit 0 is the same answer it gets for a message that landed, and the running app's CLI is 0.1.1, which has no `pane read` to check with.

**What is known and what is not.** The placeholder is measured, from a screenshot of the receiving pane. That the Return raced the paste is inference and nothing here has tested it. The threshold is unknown: 1583 bytes on one line was treated as a paste, and nothing has been sent to find where that starts, or whether it is length at all rather than arrival rate.

**This is the residue of a fix already made.** `intent.rs` sends the text and the Return as two requests on purpose: *"herdr encodes a named key against the pane's live modes and a newline in the text is just a newline - which a harness reading a bracketed paste treats as more text rather than as a submission."* So Muster already knew harnesses do bracketed-paste things with newlines. What is left is the ordering, which two requests do not fix.

## Why it is worth tracking rather than shrugging at

`pane send` exists so an agent can instruct another agent, and `docs/cli/agents.md` is built around exactly that. A send that silently does not submit turns "tell B to start" into "B is waiting for somebody to press Return", and the only symptom is an agent that never begins. An agent watching for that has nothing to watch: the state stays `idle`, which is also what it was before.

## Things that might be true

- **Say it in `muster docs limits`.** Cheapest and honest, and that file is the place: it already documents five things the CLI cannot do. Something like "a harness that shows a paste placeholder may not submit on Return, and exit 0 does not mean submitted; read the pane back to be sure". Does not need this card settled.
- **Send Return as its own request after a beat.** A delay is a guess about somebody else's input handling and would be wrong for the next harness, but it might be a guess that is right often enough to be worth its ugliness.
- **Let the caller ask.** `--enter` today is fire and forget. A `pane send --enter --confirm` that reads the pane back and says whether the text is still sitting in it would be honest, cost a round trip, and only work where the harness's input is legible.
- **Nothing.** A person driving a window presses Return themselves, and an agent that needs certainty can `pane read`. The promise in the help text would have to be softened either way.

## Add instances here

One comment per occurrence, with: the receiving harness and version, the byte count and whether the text held newlines, what the receiving pane showed, and whether the Return ever took. The interesting ones are a harness that is *not* Claude Code, and a send small enough to submit - the pair would say whether this is about length, about paste detection, or about one harness.
title: 📋 pane send --enter exits 0 without submitting, when the harness reads it as a paste
